title: Producing Rooted Cassava Plantlets for Pot Experiments
author: Matema LE Imakumbili
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z9cf92w
materials: Shoots being rooted in open plastic containers Fig

steps.title: Collect and Disinfect Stem Cuttings
steps.instruction: Collect healthy cassava stem cuttings (1 m to 1.5 m long) from mature plants using a machete.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 10% bleach solution (1 part bleach to 9 parts water) for disinfection.
Dip or wipe cutting tools in the bleach solution when moving between plants or fields.
Rinse tools in clean water after disinfection.

steps.title: Establish Nursery Beds
steps.instruction: Prepare raised nursery beds on a well-drained, flat piece of land with nutrient-poor, unfertilized soil.

substeps.instruction: Select a site typically no more than 10 m x 10 m.
Create raised beds with a width of 1 m.
Establish separate beds for each cassava variety and label them in advance.
Ensure the site is near a water source for irrigation.

steps.title: Prepare Ministem Cuttings
steps.instruction: On the day of planting, cut the long stems into ministem cuttings approximately 10 cm long.

substeps.instruction: Ensure each ministem has at least 2 nodes.
Disinfect cutting tools after each stem is cut into ministems.

steps.title: Plant Ministems
steps.instruction: Plant the ministems in the nursery beds using a 10 cm x 10 cm spacing.

substeps.instruction: Thoroughly water the nursery beds one day before planting.
Insert ministems vertically, pushing at least two-thirds of the cutting into the soil.
Place the older ends of the cuttings into the soil first so auxiliary buds face upwards.
Water the plants immediately after planting and maintain moisture by watering at least twice daily.

steps.title: Harvest Sprouted Shoots
steps.instruction: Harvest shoots in the early morning when temperatures are low once they reach approximately 15 cm in length.

substeps.instruction: Disinfect cutting tools (e.g., razor blades) using a bleach solution or alcohol when moving between plants.
Inspect plants to avoid collecting diseased material.
Place collected shoots on large papers in a shaded, aerated area to prevent dehydration.
Maintain variety labeling to avoid mixing.

steps.title: Prepare Shoots for Rooting
steps.instruction: Prepare the shoot ends and foliage immediately before placing them in rooting water.

substeps.instruction: Disinfect cutting tools.
Remove 0.5 cm to 1 cm from the initial shoot end to eliminate bruised tissue.
Make a 0.5 cm long diagonal slanted cut at the end to increase surface area for absorption.
Remove excess leaves by plucking only the leaf blades, leaving 2-3 leaves per shoot; do not pluck the petioles.

steps.title: Prepare Rooting Containers
steps.instruction: Prepare opaque containers (or cover transparent ones with opaque plastic bags) to block sunlight and prevent algae growth.

substeps.instruction: Ensure container walls are 10-12 cm high to support shoots.
Use enough containers to avoid overcrowding, which prevents shoot rot.

steps.title: Initiate Shoot Rooting
steps.instruction: Place prepared shoots into containers filled with distilled water (or cooled boiled water).

substeps.instruction: Adjust water level so shoot ends are submerged but do not float.
Lean shoots against the container edge.
Ensure leaves do not touch the water to prevent rotting.
Perform this step in a screenhouse if available.

steps.title: Manage Rooting Process
steps.instruction: Monitor shoots at least twice daily for rotting, water odor, and temperature.

substeps.instruction: Change the water daily during the first week.
After the first week, replace water every 2 to 3 days, washing containers before refilling.
Continuously trim older leaves to maintain only 2-3 leaves per shoot.
Allow roots to grow until they are 1 cm to 1.5 cm long (typically takes about 4 weeks).

steps.title: Transplant Plantlets to Pots
steps.instruction: Transplant the rooted plantlets into pots in the early morning.

substeps.instruction: Water the potting soil to field capacity and leave overnight before transplanting.
Make a 5 cm deep hole in the moist soil.
Gently place the plantlet in the hole and lightly water.
